run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T09:53:22Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is backed by a real burst of HTTP 504 error spans on its server operation "ingress": the 5-minute increase of STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans went from 0–4.5/5m before 09:53 to 60 at 09:56:22 and 105.6, 88.9, 102.0, 87.4, 30.9 through 10:06:22, while its "router frontend egress" client spans carried no error status. The sampled 504 traces are checkout flows: frontend-proxy's ingress span lasts ~15.00s (its upstream timeout) and returns 504, while the frontend's POST /api/checkout span runs ~30.0–30.1s and ends with http.status_code 200. Inside those traces checkout's PlaceOrder server span runs 30.1s because its HTTP POST client span to the email service fails after 30.0s with otel.status_description "dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout", matching checkout pod log lines "failed POST to email service: Post http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation: dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout" from 09:53:43 to 10:01:01. Chaos-mesh events show NetworkChaos experiments named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-* applying chaos to both email pods and the checkout pod from 09:53:12 onward, spawned each minute by a Schedule of the same base name in namespace chaos-mesh; the alert anchor 09:53:22 is 10s after the first "Experiment has started" event. All otel-demo deployments stayed Ready (1/1, email 2/2) and all pods stayed Running with restart count 0, so the fault is a network-level partition on the checkout→email path, not a crash, restart or rollout. Unresolved: the alerting rule itself was not returned by Prometheus (so the exact 0.2444 value/window is unverified), events stop at 10:00:12, and email-side application logs could not be read.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's STATUS_CODE_ERROR span increase (5m) on operation "ingress" was 2.5, 4.5, 2.2, 0, 0, 1.1, 3.3, 2.2, 0 and 2.2 at the 2-minute points from 09:36:22 to 09:54:22, then jumped to 60 at 09:56:22, 105.6 at 09:58:22, 88.9 at 10:00:22, 102.0 at 10:02:22, 87.4 at 10:04:22 and 30.9 at 10:06:22; the "router frontend egress" operation showed 0 error increase throughout.

Sampled frontend-proxy error spans are operation "ingress" with error=true, http.status_code 504 and otel.status_code ERROR, duration 15,000,082–15,001,444 microseconds, each parented to a load-generator POST span that also carries http.status_code 504 and error=true.

The 504 traces are checkout requests: frontend span "POST /api/checkout" runs 30,012,991–30,128,383 microseconds and ends http.status_code 200, its child "grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" runs 30,012,312–30,125,883 microseconds with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, and checkout's own "oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder" server span runs 30,011,218–30,124,909 microseconds. The load-generator's POST span for the same request is a 504, so frontend-proxy timed out at ~15s before the ~30s frontend/checkout response completed.

checkout's erroring "HTTP POST" client spans last 30,000,161–30,000,648 microseconds and carry otel.status_code ERROR with otel.status_description exactly "dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout"; this HTTP POST span is a child of checkout's PlaceOrder span.

The checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs logged repeated lines "failed to send order confirmation to \"<user>@example.com\": failed POST to email service: Post \"http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation\": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout", first seen 2026-11-17T09:53:43.627798237Z and continuing through 2026-11-17T10:01:01.730908027Z in the lines returned (97 matching lines).

Chaos-mesh events record NetworkChaos object otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-jdmmj with "Experiment has started" and "Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn", "...email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w" and "...checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs" at 2026-11-17T09:53:12Z, then TimeUp at 09:54:07Z and Recovered for the same three pods; further NetworkChaos instances (hddgv, mznpj, zl9p2, 7rvkf, 8p7rs, 4f5lv, 5c2dr) repeat the same start/apply ~55s/recover cycle each minute through 10:00:12Z.

Schedule object otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh emitted "Create new object: otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-<suffix>" (reason Spawned) plus lastScheduleTime updates every minute from 2026-11-17T09:53:12Z to 2026-11-17T10:00:12Z, matching the NetworkChaos instance names and times.

Error-span increases across the whole authorized window show only frontend-proxy and checkout materially elevated: frontend-proxy 105.6 (09:58:22 point) and 110 (10:03:22 point) per 5m, checkout 37.9 and 60 per 5m, while ad, fraud-detection and recommendation each show only isolated 1.11 values and no email series is returned.

All 22 otel-demo pods were Running with container ready=true and restartCount 0 at query time, including frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-jft59, checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn; all deployments report replicas=ready=available (frontend-proxy 1/1/1, checkout 1/1/1, email 2/2/2) with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-*, and the pods are owned by ReplicaSets and started 09:20:02–09:20:05Z, i.e. before the incident window.

The Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition (namespace chaos-mesh) is the object that originated the fault: its Spawned events name each NetworkChaos instance, and those NetworkChaos instances are the objects whose events record chaos being applied to email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn and checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs starting 09:53:12Z, 10 seconds before the alert anchor 09:53:22Z.

The email service kept serving during the incident: its server span "POST /send_order_confirmation" increase per 2m was 66.7–77.3 at 09:53–09:55 and 48–57.3 at 09:56–10:03, i.e. email continued to receive traffic rather than being down.

frontend-proxy itself was not crashed, restarted or rescheduled: its pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-jft59 was Running/Ready with restartCount 0, its deployment was 1/1 available, and it started at 09:20:05Z; no otel-demo pod create/delete events appear in the events sample.

checkout's other dependencies were not failing in the sampled error traces: oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge (505–1558us), oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert (517–14890us), oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and /EmptyCart (349–4286us), oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (73–1578us) and shipping /get-quote and /ship-order (37–1936us) all returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0; the only erroring client span is the 30s HTTP POST to email.

Small frontend-proxy error counts existed before the deviation (2.5 and 4.5 per 5m at 09:36:22 and 09:38:22, 1.1–3.3 at 09:44:22–09:54:22), so the background error level was near zero but nonzero; the alert-relevant change is the rise to 60–105 per 5m from 09:56:22, not the pre-existing background.

Mechanism: the NetworkChaos experiments spawned by Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition drop packets between the checkout pod and the email pods, so checkout's POST to email:8080 hangs in TCP connect until the 30s dial timeout, checkout's PlaceOrder takes ~30s, the frontend's /api/checkout takes ~30s, and frontend-proxy's ~15s upstream timeout turns those requests into ingress 504s, which is what the RequestErrorRate alert measures. The fault named by the chaos object (email↔checkout network partition) matches the failing path (checkout→email dial i/o timeout) and the affected pod names exactly.

Rejected: the email service was down or unhealthy, causing the timeouts. Email deployment was 2/2 ready, both email pods were Running/Ready with restartCount 0, email's own server spans continued (48–57.3 per 2m at 09:56–10:03), and the observed failure is a dial timeout (dropped SYN) rather than connection refused.

Rejected: a rollout, restart or rescheduling of frontend-proxy, frontend, checkout or email caused the errors. All four workloads' deployments were fully ready, their pods started at 09:20:02–09:20:05Z, restart counts were 0, and no otel-demo Pod SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete/Killing events appear in the events sample.

Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition and its spawned NetworkChaos objects; if this fault injection is not intended, suspend or delete the Schedule (which stops the per-minute NetworkChaos instances) and confirm the checkout→email path recovers.

Make checkout's order-confirmation call to email asynchronous or bound it well below frontend-proxy's ~15s upstream timeout, so a slow or unreachable email service cannot make otherwise successful checkout requests exceed the proxy timeout and turn into 504s.

gaps: The Alertmanager alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data), so the rule expression, evaluation window and the reported current value 0.2444444444444444 could not be verified against Prometheus.

Events are only present through 2026-11-17T10:00:12Z (source_end_at 10:00:28Z), so whether the Schedule kept spawning NetworkChaos instances and whether the checkout→email partition was still active after 10:00 is unknown; an instant error-rate query at 10:10:00Z returned no data (metric samples end around 10:06:22Z), so whether the frontend-proxy errors continued past ~10:06 is unknown.

The chaos-mesh Schedule/NetworkChaos object specs could not be read (those kinds are not available to the Kubernetes query tool), so the partition's exact selectors, direction and duration are inferred from event messages ("Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/<pod>", TimeUp ~55s after start) and not from the object spec.

NetworkPolicy objects could not be evaluated: the networkpolicies query returned no items with status no_data (not citable), so a policy-based block on the checkout→email path can be neither confirmed nor excluded from this data.

Email-side application logs could not be checked: fetch_pod_logs for email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w returned no lines (status no_data), so email's own application-level errors are unknown; email health was assessed only from pod status, deployment readiness and its continuing server spans.

kube-state-metrics series kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="otel-demo"} and kube_pod_owner{namespace="otel-demo",...} returned no data at 2026-11-17T10:06:00Z, so workload status was taken from the Kubernetes API objects instead.

No pre-09:53 latency baseline was established for frontend-proxy ingress spans, so this report makes no latency-trend claim; the 15s 504 spans and 30s frontend/checkout spans are reported as absolute observations only.

Whether the frontend-proxy 504s affected requests other than checkout flows could not be established: only checkout POST traces were among the sampled 504 traces, and a full breakdown of ingress 504s by request target was not available.
next_steps: Inspect (read-only) the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition and the NetworkChaos specs it spawns to confirm selectors, direction (checkout↔email) and duration against the observed 55s cycles.
Confirm with the team whether this partition experiment is intentional; if not, plan to suspend the Schedule and verify that checkout's "dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout" log lines stop.
Decouple or time-bound checkout's synchronous POST to http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation so it cannot exceed frontend-proxy's ~15s upstream timeout.
Re-check frontend-proxy ingress error rate and checkout email-POST errors after 10:06:22Z, since current Prometheus samples end there and the post-10:00 state is unverified.
